Higher is better.The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better.Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better.Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better.

The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.ModelCorrect recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better.of 2,069 pairs(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better.0–100Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better.error, pointsOf the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better.caught · false alarmsThe mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under itClient wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better.median, p90 under itInput tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better.$ per 1,000 pairsMeasured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.ModelExpected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better.error, points(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better.0–100Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better.of 2,069 pairsOf the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better.caught · false alarmsThe mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under itClient wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better.median, p90 under itInput tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better.$ per 1,000 pairsMeasured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better.s per 1,000 pairs

An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better.caught · false alarms(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better.0–100Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better.of 2,069 pairsExpected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better.error, pointsThe mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under itClient wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Lower is better.median, p90 under itInput tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. Lower is better.$ per 1,000 pairsMeasured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.ModelThe mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under it(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better.0–100Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better.of 2,069 pairsExpected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better.error, pointsOf the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better.caught · false alarmsClient wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better.median, p90 under itInput tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.ModelClient wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better.median, p90 under it(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better.0–100Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better.of 2,069 pairsExpected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better.error, pointsOf the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better.caught · false alarmsThe mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under itInput tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better.$ per 1,000 pairsMeasured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better.s per 1,000 pairs

The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.ModelInput tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better.$ per 1,000 pairs(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better.0–100Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better.of 2,069 pairsExpected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better.error, pointsOf the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better.caught · false alarmsThe mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under itClient wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better.median, p90 under itMeasured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better.s per 1,000 pairs

The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.ModelMeasured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better.s per 1,000 pairs(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better.0–100Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better.of 2,069 pairsExpected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better.error, pointsOf the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better.caught · false alarmsThe mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better.0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under itClient wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better.median, p90 under itInput tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Nemotron-Labs-Sigma-3B-instruct · NVIDIA

Open · 3.0B

nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Sigma-3B-instruct@057a0843, BF16, a local OpenAI-compatible wrapper, sigma_server.py (Transformers custom code, DDIM 32 steps per 32-token block, guidance 3, score temperature 0.3; one request at a time per copy) on one RTX PRO 6000 (ours), self-hosted; the wrapper makes two local fixes to the release's loading. It builds the noise schedule from the checkpoint's own projected_bernstein tensors, because the release's config builds a legacy schedule that leaves them unused. Its stop check reads special tokens, because the release's decode skips its own end-of-turn token. The server's per-reply sampler record was not kept by our client; one question per request, 5 requests at a time (latency not comparable across different concurrency); the server also answered another benchmark's requests (Reading) for part of the run, so its latency and GPU time are shared-load figures; thinking off; answer rule v2: the label is the last marker 'ANSWER: X' anywhere in the visible reply, where the word ANSWER may be in any letter case and X must be an uppercase A, B or C; the reasoning text is never read; v2 replaced rule v1 (the word in uppercase only) on 15 Nov after v1 was found to miss replies written 'Answer: X', and applies to every chat row; 436 of 2069 replies (21%) had no answer marker and count wrong (0 of them cut off at the 8,192-token context (prompt plus reply; the server caps each reply at 8,192 minus its prompt in the model's own tokens)); every reply kept; before the run, 1 published-cohort pair was sent in test requests whose outputs were not kept, so its scored row comes from a later request

Hardware: one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB), ours
